messages:
alice: Seeing a weird spike during canary: enabling the fused-flash attention + fp8 quant path in the runtime produced a cluster of NaNs in downstream logits. Repro on small repro harness available.

bob: Ugh. Did you also switch paged-KV on for that canary? We recently enabled paging heuristics for long-context runs.

alice: Yes—paged-KV was on. Batch size 8, seq_len=4096, kv page size default. Error shows up after ~300 tokens.

carol: Can you paste the exact log snippet? Is it softmax -> exp overflow or something earlier?

alice: Log: 
```
2026-03-17 12:34:58,123 serve INFO token 312: logits contains INF
Runtime: fused_flash_attn_fp8_v2 selected
KV: paged
Tensor stats: qk_scale max=1.2e4, softmax_pre_max=12345.6, softmax_exp sum=inf
```

bob: That softmax_pre_max number looks huge. Maybe quantization scale mismatch when pages get concatenated? If fp8 scaling isn't recomputed across pages we could overflow the exp.

dan: I ran a quick perf profile with perfkit: the fused kernel takes over fallback path at token 300, then we see a sudden jump in qk scale when KV page boundary is crossed. Attn kernel has a branch that skips rescaling on page append.

carol: Repro command I used: `python -m tests.repro.attn_repro --model small --seq 4096 --batch 8 --mode fused --dtype fp8 --kv paged`

alice: Adding failure repro here: `attach: /tmp/repro_fp8_paged.tar.gz` (small harness and seed).

bob: Quick mitigation: set softmax clamp in runtime to protect exp: clamp_exp_input = min(max(x, -50), 50). That avoids INF but may hide correctness issue. Do we want a hotfix?

dan: Hotfix LGTM for canary rollback. But root cause probably is inconsistent scaling factors across page boundaries. fp8 stores per-tensor scale metadata; when pages are concatenated we should recompute relative scale or convert to a common internal float buffer before softmax.

carol: I pushed a branch `fix/kv-page-scale-normalize` that forces dequantization to BF16 before concatenation and applies a stable softmax with max-shift across entire sequence. Need someone to run CI perf/accuracy.

alice: Ran that branch quickly — numeric stable, no NaNs. Latency regress ~3% vs fused fp8 path, but still way faster than full bf16 fused. Accuracy looked identical on our eval prompts.

bob: Perf note: the runtime kernel selector currently prefers fused_fp8 when throughput < threshold and pages<2, but the paging heuristic didn't count page-appends at runtime. We should update selector to prefer bf16-fused if pages>1 until scale normalization is cheap.

dan: Agreed. Also worth adding an assert in debug builds that checks for Inf/NaN after softmax and prints qk_scale and per-page max before catastrophic blowup. That will help catch regressions earlier.

carol: Adding a microbench: run fused_fp8 + paged vs fused_bf16 + paged across seqs [512,1024,2048,4096] with batch=1 and record max qk pre-softmax. I'll post numbers in this thread.

alice: FYI infra-bot flagged canary and rolled back the canary deployment at 12:36. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed for job runtime-canary-21 at 2026-03-17T12:36:05Z.

bob: Next steps: (1) merge normalize-deq branch as opt-in behind config flag, (2) update kernel selector heuristics to avoid fused_fp8 when paged-KV active, (3) add softmax guardrails and debug asserts, (4) run full eval on devbench.

carol: I'll open PRs for 1+3. Dan can you take selector change?

dan: On it. I'll also add telemetry to capture qk_scale distribution and page-count at selection time so we can tune thresholds empirically.

alice: Thanks team — that matches my plan. Leaving the repro and perf artifacts in the shared folder: `s3://redwood-ci/attn-repro/1812345678/`.

bob: One more thought: fp8 dynamic range choices differ between formats (e4m3 vs e5m2). We were defaulting to e5m2 for throughput, which has smaller mantissa. Might be worth switching to e4m3 for attention ops where softmax sensitivity is high. Add that to the evaluation matrix.

carol: Good call. I'll add e4m3/e5m2 axes to the perf/accuracy matrix.

alice: Great. Closing loop once PRs are in and CI passes.
